app.ask.answer.data: Ask panel short answer to privacy questions. "Sign out" and "shelf" must use the same words as the Sign out button and the shelf elsewhere in the app.
app.ask.answer.howLong: Ask panel short answer to deadline questions. "Window" is the label of a row on the rule page; use that row label's translation.
app.ask.answer.legal: Ask panel short answer to legal questions. "Owed" is the brand name: do not translate it.
app.ask.answer.script: Ask panel short answer. "Get script" is a button label; use that button's translation.
app.ask.bestLead: Ask panel answer when no specific answer matched. {title} = a rule title (may be in English). Use your language's quotation marks. "window" = the claim deadline row, "script" = the words to say.
app.ask.noItem: "Help" is the Help page link label; use its translation.
app.ask.ruleLine: Ask panel answer line naming a rule. {title} = the rule title, {clause} = the start of what the rule gives you. Both come from the rulebook and may be in English.
app.ask.seed.howLong: Starter question button (see app.ask.seed.receipt). Must NOT contain any word of the receipt, legal, data or free answers (they are tried first). French must contain one of: combien de temps, délai, date limite, échéance, expire, trop tard, en retard (e.g. "Combien de temps ai-je ?"). Spanish must contain one of: cuánto tiempo, plazo, fecha límite, vence, vencimiento, caduca, expira (e.g. "¿Cuánto tiempo tengo?").
app.ask.seed.receipt: Starter question button in the Ask panel. Clicking it sends this exact text as the question, and without an on-device AI the answer is picked by words in it. French must contain one of: reçu, ticket, facture, preuve, relevé (e.g. "Ai-je besoin de mon reçu ?"). Spanish must contain one of: recibo, ticket, factura, comprobante, prueba (e.g. "¿Necesito mi recibo?").
app.ask.seed.script: Starter question button (see app.ask.seed.receipt). Must NOT contain any word of the receipt, legal, data, free or deadline answers (they are tried first). French must contain one of: dire, dis, appeler, appel, téléphone, courriel, email, mail (e.g. "Que dois-je dire au téléphone ?"). Spanish must contain one of: decir, digo, diga, llamar, llamada, teléfono, correo, email (e.g. "¿Qué digo por teléfono?").
app.card.by: Deadline chip on a rule row: the claim must be made by this date. {date} = a date already written in your language ("2 November 2026"); write the preposition that fits it (FR e.g. "Avant le {date}", ES "Antes del {date}").
app.card.dateUnknown: Not shown today. A rule with a time limit, when the person does not know when they bought the item.
app.card.getScript: Button on each rule row: opens the words to say to the company (the claim script). The Ask panel answer app.ask.answer.script names this button, so keep the two identical.
app.card.src.manufacturer: Short source word on each rule row, all app.card.src.* keys: who gives the cover. Shown before the start of the rule's window text, joined with " · ", e.g. "The maker · One year from the day you bought it…". manufacturer = the brand's own warranty; card = the credit card used to pay; settlement = money from a class-action settlement; program = a maker's free repair programme; statutory = consumer law; retailer = the shop that sold it; other = a source Owed has no word for. Two or three words, capitalised as a label.
app.card.startHere: Small badge on the first, best rule in the results.
app.corpus.count: Small note in the top bar: how many rules Owed knows, when under 100 (in practice there are always more). "the book" = Owed's rulebook. English writes "rules" even for 1 (kept as it is); give your language a real singular.
app.corpus.failed: Small note in the top bar when the list of rules failed to download. Short: the top bar is narrow.
app.corpus.over: Small note in the top bar, a round figure: {count} is a multiple of 100 ("300"), and the meaning is "more than 300 rules". Write it your language's way, e.g. FR "Plus de {count} règles". Short: the top bar is narrow.
app.demo.name: Display name given to the demo account the first time ?demo=1 is opened. It is saved with the account, so it stays in the language it was created in.
app.doc.contact: Row label in a rule's details: phone number, web page or email to claim through.
app.doc.deadline: Row label in a rule's details and in the claim script: the last date to claim.
app.doc.explainer: Row label in a rule's details: a link to an outside organisation's plain-language page about the same law (e.g. "The Repair Association: California").
app.doc.getWords: Main button at the bottom of a rule's details panel: opens the claim script.
app.doc.howToClaim: Heading above a rule's numbered steps.
app.doc.kicker: Small label at the top of the rule's details panel, beside the strength tag.
app.doc.source: Row label in a rule's details: the link to the official text of the rule.
app.doc.why: Last line of a rule's details. {reason} = one to four lowercase clauses joined as a list (the engine.reason.* keys, e.g. "it is a Sony item and you are still inside the window"). "it" is the rule. FR needs a no-break space before the colon.
app.doc.window: Row label in a rule's details: how long the person has to claim (the time window, not a glass window; FR "Délai", ES "Plazo"). The Ask panel answer app.ask.answer.howLong names this row, so keep the two identical.
app.filter.empty.strong: Message when the results filter chip Strong / Worth asking / Long shot (app.filter.empty.strong / .worth / .longshot) hides every rule for this item. "this one" = the item, whose gender is unknown (FR e.g. "pour cet objet"). "All" is the first filter chip's label: use exactly that chip's translation. {count} = how many rules matched in total (the ones All shows); "the {count} that did match" agrees with it. The strength words should match the chips' translations (app.strength.*).
app.item.brandCategory: Fallback name of a thing when the user typed none, e.g. "Sony Headphones". {brand} = brand, {category} = the category label as shown in the question 1 tiles (capitalised). Put the noun first if your language does ("{category} {brand}"). This name is saved with the thing.
app.link.newTab: Screen-reader only, read straight after the text of a link that opens in a new tab ("Read the rule (opens in a new tab)"). Plain text; the space before it is added by the app.
app.photo.barcode: {code} = the digits read from a barcode. HTML: keep <b>.
app.photo.condition.looksNew: Condition of the photographed thing, lowercase, shown in the list after "From the photo:". The thing's noun (and its gender) is not known, so prefer a form that does not need to agree with it.
app.photo.hint.phone: Where a model number is found, per kind of thing (all app.photo.hint.* keys). Plain text, no < or &. Each is used in TWO places and must read correctly in both: after "it is" in app.photo.noModel ("it" = the model number, so any participle agrees with "model number": French "numéro" masc., Spanish "número" masc.), and after "Where the model number hides:" in app.photo.whereModel. Menu names (Settings, About, About This Mac, System) should match the phone or computer's own menus in your language.
app.photo.kind.headphones: Everyday word for a thing seen in a photo (all app.photo.kind.* keys), lowercase, used as {kind} in the name templates (app.photo.name.*), e.g. "Sony headphones". A few ids are one word cut from a longer name, and the name shows only that word: kind.washing and kind.washer = washing machine, kind.machine = coffee/washing machine, kind.coffee = coffee machine, kind.air and kind.conditioner = air conditioner (kind.air also appears for chairs, an existing bug), kind.hob = cooktop, kind.trainers = sneakers. Translate each as the whole thing.
app.photo.name.brandModel: Name written into the name field from a photo, e.g. "Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones". {brand} and {model} are read off the item; {kind} = app.photo.kind.* (lowercase). Reorder for your language ("{kind} {brand} {model}"). Saved as the thing's name.
app.photo.name.colour: Name from a photo when no brand or model was readable, e.g. "black headphones". {colour} is the on-device AI's English colour word (it is not translated), {kind} = app.photo.kind.*.
app.photo.noModel: Photo note when no model number was readable. {hint} = where the model number usually is (app.photo.hint.*), e.g. "on the back of the case"; "it" = the model number. HTML: keep <b> and the <button ... data-paste> element exactly (attributes unchanged, only its text translated); the button pastes the clipboard into the name field.
app.photo.seen: Note under the photo. {seen} = what was recognised, joined with " · ": the name (app.photo.name.*), a condition word (app.photo.condition.*) and short features read by the on-device AI (those stay English). HTML: keep <b>.
app.photo.serial: Sentence added to the photo note when a serial number was read. HTML: keep <b>.
app.photo.unsure: Note under the photo on question 1. HTML: keep the <b> tags. Do not use a bare < or &.
app.photo.whereModel: Photo note on phones without on-device AI. {hint} = app.photo.hint.* (a place). HTML: keep <b> and the <button ... data-paste> element exactly, only its text translated.
app.print.note: Footer of the printed claim. {date} = today, already written in your language (e.g. "16 September 2026"). "Owed" is the brand name.
app.print.serial: On the printed claim, one of the facts under the heading. {serial} = serial number.
app.rail.soonest: Side panel summary. {date} = a formatted date, {name} = the name of the user's thing (typed by the user, any gender).
app.region.placeInCountry: Region pill in the top bar when a province or state is picked. {place} = province/state name, {country} = country name, e.g. "Ontario, Canada". Space is tight (it truncates).
app.region.set: Toast after changing region. {place} is a bare place name ("Ontario", "United States (any state)") with no article. If your language needs an article or preposition that depends on the place, use a label form such as "Region: {place}".
app.rename.done: Toast after renaming a saved thing. The thing's gender is unknown; prefer a neutral wording.
app.results.failed: Results area when the list of rules could not be downloaded. HTML: keep ... (the bold part shows as its own line, so no space is needed after ). "the rulebook" = Owed's list of warranty and consumer rules. "serve them over http" is advice for a developer who opened the files straight from disk.
app.results.fold.hide: Fallback label of an open fold button; practically never shown (app.results.fold.hideWorth / hideLong are used).
app.results.fold.hideLong: The same button once the "Long shots" group is open. Plain text in an attribute: no double quotes.
app.results.fold.hideWorth: The same button once the "Worth asking" group is open (it folds it again). Plain text in an attribute: no double quotes.
app.results.fold.longNote: Not shown today (kept for a folded group's description). Describes rules marked "Long shot": they probably do not apply to the person, but are listed anyway.
app.results.fold.showLong: Button that unfolds the group headed "Long shots" (app.strength.longshot.plural). {count} = how many rules are in it; the noun and adjective agree with it.
app.results.fold.showWorth: Button that unfolds the group headed "Worth asking" (app.strength.worth.plural). {count} = how many rules are in it. English uses the tag words as a noun; write a natural phrase, e.g. FR "Afficher {count} règle(s) à vérifier" split into one/other.
app.results.fold.worthNote: Not shown today (kept for a folded group's description). Describes rules marked "Worth asking".
app.results.loading: Results area while the list of rules is still downloading. HTML: keep ... (shown as its own line).
app.results.serial: In the facts line under the results title, after the category, brand and age, joined with " · ". "S/N" abbreviates serial number; {serial} is the number as typed. Keep it short.
app.results.summary.ask: Big one-line summary at the top of the results. {count} = how many places (maker, card, shop, law...) may owe the person a repair; the whole sentence is chosen by the number, so make the verb agree too. HTML: keep {count} exactly (the number is bold); the number may move within the sentence.
app.results.summary.none: Results summary when no rule is a good fit (only weak matches, or rules to double-check). A "lead" is a rule that may get the person a free repair.
app.results.summary.onlyLong: Results summary when the only matches are long shots (general rules that probably do not apply). Use the same word as app.strength.longshot.plural.
app.rule.englishOnly: Quiet line at the top of a rule's details when that rule has no checked translation, so its title, steps and window are shown in English. Never shown on the English site.
app.rule.read: Link to the official page a rule comes from (a law, a warranty page). An arrow icon follows it.
app.script.asked: Button: the person marks that they have sent the claim to the company ("them").
app.script.askedToast: Notice after I asked them. "It" = this claim.
app.script.backToResults: Screen-reader label of the back arrow on the claim script (narrow screens). Plain text in an attribute: no double quotes.
app.script.backToRule: Back button at the top of the claim script on wide screens (a left arrow comes first): goes back to the rule's details. May be a different word from app.script.rule if your language needs one ("back to the rule").
app.script.copied: The Copy script button's label for a moment after copying (the script was copied).
app.script.copiedToast: Short spoken/visible notice after copying the script.
app.script.copy: Button: copies the claim script. It briefly changes to app.script.copied and then back to this.
app.script.heading: Heading of the claim script view.
app.script.help: Help line under the claim script. "it" = the script; "their" = the company's.
app.script.kicker: Small label at the top of the claim script view. "script" = the words to say to the company.
app.script.rule: Row label above the claim script: the rule's title follows, then a "Read the rule" link.
app.script.send: Button: opens the person's email app, or the company's page or phone, with the script copied. "it" = the script.
app.script.sentLink: Notice after Send it, when the company is reached through a web page that just opened. "Words" = the script; "their" = the company's.
app.script.sentOther: Notice after Send it, when the rule names no phone, email or page to contact: the rule's official page is opened instead. "Their" = the company's.
app.script.sentPhone: Notice after Send it, when the company's contact is a phone number. {phone} = the number as written in the rule (e.g. "1-800-275-2273"). FR may need "le {phone}", ES "al {phone}". "them" = the copied words.
app.script.subject: Email subject line when sending the script. {title} = the rule's title, in the rule's own language (often English). Nothing may agree with {title}: prefer a label form such as FR "Réclamation : {title}" over one where a preposition must contract with its article.
app.script.subjectItem: The same subject when the item has a name. {name} = the item's name as the person typed it. See app.script.subject.
app.script.who: Row label above the claim script: who to contact (a phone number, web page or email follows). One short word or label.
app.script.won: Button: the person marks that the claim succeeded. The implied noun is the claim (FR "réclamation", ES "reclamación").
app.script.wonToast: Notice after Mark as won: the item gets repaired instead of thrown away. "the bin" = the rubbish bin / trash; use your language's everyday idiom.
app.shelf.newRules: Toast once per visit. {count} = how many rules newly match the things on the shelf.
app.shelf.remove: Screen-reader label of the X button on a shelf row. {name} = the thing's name. No double quotes (it sits in an attribute).
app.shelf.removed: Toast after removing a thing. {name} is typed by the user (unknown gender); prefer a wording that does not agree with it, e.g. "Removed from your shelf: {name}".
app.shelf.showMore: Button under the shelf list; {count} = how many more things are hidden.
app.shelf.status.ask: Tooltip on a shelf row: {count} = how many rules are worth asking about for this thing. Every counted phrase from app.js writes its number as {count}, not {n} (English keeps plain digits there); the plural form is picked from the same number.
app.shelf.status.askAfterNumber: Screen-reader text read straight after the visible number on a shelf row (the number is shown separately just before it). Keep the leading space. It must read naturally after the number, e.g. "3" + " to ask". Plain text, no quotes.
app.shelf.status.long: Tooltip on a shelf row when only long shots matched ("Long shot" = a rule that probably does not apply).
app.shelf.status.longAfterNumber: Screen-reader text read straight after the visible number (see app.shelf.status.askAfterNumber). Keep the leading space.
app.side.claim.asked: Status of a claim the user sent, lowercase, in the sidebar: "asked · 16 Sep". The implied noun is "claim" (French "réclamation", Spanish "reclamación"); agree with it.
app.side.daysLeft: After a deadline date and " · ": "2 November 2026 · 3 days left". {count} = days. Lowercase start.
app.side.dueToday: Lowercase, after a date and " · ": "2 November 2026 · today" (the deadline is today).
app.signOut.confirm:
Browser confirm dialog. Keep the line breaks (

 after the question, 
 between the last two lines). OK clears the list; Cancel keeps it. The browser draws the Cancel button in ITS OWN language, which may differ from the page, so naming the button is risky: consider "Cancel" in the browser's wording or describing it ("the other button").
app.strength.longshot.word: Strength tag: a general rule that probably does not apply. Short pill text.
app.strength.strong.key: One-line explanation under a rule title for this strength.
app.strength.strong.plural: Plural form of the tag word, for a heading over several rules of this strength (shown as the heading of a folded group of results).
app.strength.strong.word: Strength tag on a rule (a lead the user can claim). One of three: Strong / Worth asking / Long shot. Shown in a small pill; keep it short. It describes a rule or lead (French "piste/règle", Spanish "pista/regla").
app.strength.worth.word: Strength tag: the rule fits but one thing needs checking. Short pill text.
appShell.ask.grip: Tooltip on the drag handle of the floating question panel. 'Shift' is the keyboard key; use the name printed on keyboards in your language.
appShell.ask.note: Intro at the top of the question panel. 'Owed' is the brand; 'rulebook' is its collection of rules.
appShell.ask.placeholder: Placeholder in the question box: an example question. Keep it the same question as the Help dialog's appShell.helpDialog.receiptQ and the app's suggested question buttons.
appShell.ask.title: Both the sidebar row that opens the question panel and that panel's title.
appShell.brand.home: Screen-reader name of the brand logo link that goes to the Owed home page. 'Owed' is the brand name.
appShell.camera.note: Instruction on the camera sheet. The app also sets this same text again after the camera starts; keep both identical.
appShell.camera.shoot: Shutter button that captures the photo now. Different from appShell.photo.take ('Take a photo', which opens the camera).
appShell.help: Used for every 'Help' in the app: the phone Help tab, sidebar link and its tooltip, the Help dialog title, the corner '?' link name and a footer link. Keep it one short word.
appShell.helpDialog.credit: HTML. Keep the <a ...> tag and all its attributes exactly; you may move it within the sentence. 'The Repair Association' is an organisation's proper name, keep it in English. 'State' = US state.
appShell.helpDialog.freeA: 'No cut of anything you claim' = Owed takes no commission on what you get back.
appShell.helpDialog.receiptA: 'Not to check' = you do not need the receipt to check your item in Owed.
appShell.meta.title: Browser tab title of the app page. 'Owed' is the brand, keep it. 'Shelf' is the user's saved list of things they own; use the same word as in every other 'shelf' string. The spaced dash separator may follow your language's convention.
appShell.nav.label: Screen-reader name of the sidebar navigation. 'Shelf' = the user's saved list of things they own.
appShell.nav.start: Sidebar row that opens the start screen (the first question of a new check). A noun-like nav label, like 'Home'.
appShell.photo.add: Button that opens the file picker to choose a photo of the item.
appShell.photo.remove: Removes the chosen photo from the form. Nothing is deleted.
appShell.photo.take: Button that opens the camera, and the camera sheet's screen-reader name. Different from appShell.camera.shoot ('Take the photo', the shutter).
appShell.rail.beforeCall: Checklist heading: what to have ready before calling the seller or maker.
appShell.rail.longShotDesc: Explains the 'Long shot' tag shown just before it: a general rule that probably does not apply to you.
appShell.rail.strongDesc: Explains the 'Strong' tag shown just before it.
appShell.rail.worthDesc: Explains the 'Worth asking' tag shown just before it. The subject is the rule.
appShell.region.loading: Short note under the region pill while Owed loads its rules. 'Rulebook' = Owed's collection of warranty and repair rules; use the same word everywhere.
appShell.region.newYork: The US state, not the city.
appShell.region.otherProvince: Dropdown option under Canada: a Canadian province not in the list.
appShell.region.otherState: Dropdown option under United States: a US state not in the list.
appShell.region.us: Group label for US states in the 'Where you live' dropdown, and the first-paint text of the region pill. The app may show it after a state name, as in 'California, United States'.
appShell.results.edit: Button that reopens the four questions to change the answers for this item.
appShell.results.filterAll: Filter tab showing all matching rules. A count is shown right after it.
appShell.results.noneBody: 'It' in the second sentence is the user's item. 'if a rule lands' = if a matching rule is added later. 'Rulebook' and 'shelf' must match their other uses.
appShell.results.noneTitle: Shown when no rule matches the item. 'this one' = this item.
appShell.results.rename: Tooltip on the same pencil button.
appShell.results.renameLabel: Screen-reader name of the pencil button that renames the saved item.
appShell.results.titlePlaceholder: First-paint placeholder for the results title; the app replaces it with the user's item before it is shown. An example item: brand 'Sony' + the category 'headphones'. Keep 'Sony'.
appShell.script.heading: Screen-reader heading of the page with the ready-to-use text the user says or sends to claim a repair.
appShell.shelf.label: Heading of the collapsible list of items the user saved. Must agree with the phone tab 'Saved' (appShell.tabs.saved).
appShell.shelf.showMore: First-paint label of the button under the saved list. The app replaces it with a counted label once it knows how many items are hidden.
appShell.side.checkNew: Main sidebar button that starts checking a new item for free repairs.
appShell.side.comingUp: Sidebar block heading over upcoming claim deadlines. Shown in uppercase by CSS.
appShell.side.recent: Sidebar block heading over rules the user recently opened.
appShell.strength.longShot: Match strength of a rule: a general rule that probably does not apply. Filter tab and legend tag; keep it short.
appShell.strength.strong: Match strength of a rule: it fits what the user told us. Used on a filter tab (followed by a count) and on a coloured tag in the ranking legend. Refers to rules.
appShell.strength.worth: Match strength of a rule: it fits, with one thing to check, so it is worth asking the seller or maker. Filter tab and legend tag; keep it short.
appShell.summary.strong: Small lowercase label under a number in the sidebar summary: how many rules are strong matches. Same idea as appShell.strength.strong. Any count.
appShell.summary.things: Small lowercase label under a number in the sidebar summary (number of saved items). The number is any count and is shown separately above, so pick a form that reads for any number.
appShell.summary.won: Small lowercase label under a number in the sidebar summary: how many claims the user won. Any count.
appShell.tabs.label: Screen-reader name of the phone's bottom tab bar (main navigation).
appShell.tabs.new: Phone bottom tab that starts a new check of an item. Very narrow.
appShell.tabs.saved: Phone bottom tab showing the saved items. Very narrow; must agree with appShell.shelf.label.
appShell.util.signOut: Button and its tooltip. There is no real account: it forgets the name stored in this browser. The Ask panel's canned answers refer to this button by name, so keep them consistent.
appShell.util.theme: Label next to the light/dark appearance toggle.
appShell.wizard.back: Back button in the four-question flow (both the icon button's screen-reader name and the footer button).
appShell.wizard.brandNotListed: Toggle that reveals a text box to type a brand that is not among the brand buttons. 'it' = the brand.
appShell.wizard.brandPlaceholder: Placeholder in the brand box. Keep 'Sony'; translate 'e.g.'.
appShell.wizard.broken: Checkbox label: the item is currently broken. 'It' is the item, gender unknown.
appShell.wizard.countFirst: First-paint step counter. The app replaces it with the live step number as the user moves through the questions.
appShell.wizard.help4: Some credit cards extend warranties / cover repairs.
appShell.wizard.modelPlaceholder: Placeholder in a narrow text box. Keep the example product name 'iPhone 14 Plus' as is; translate the rest and the 'e.g.' abbreviation.
appShell.wizard.photoInstead: Toggle that reveals the typed-model and photo options instead of picking a tile. Different from appShell.photo.add.
appShell.wizard.q1: Question 1 heading; the user picks the kind of item (phone, laptop, headphones...). The item's gender is unknown, so avoid wording that needs it.
appShell.wizard.q2: Question 2 heading: the brand of the item. 'it' is the item, whose gender is unknown; rephrasing around 'brand' is fine.
appShell.wizard.q3: Question 3 heading: roughly when the item was bought. 'it' is the item, gender unknown; rephrasing around the purchase is fine.
appShell.wizard.serialLabel: Screen-reader name of the serial number box. Its placeholder is appShell.wizard.serialPlaceholder (worded slightly differently in English).
appShell.wizard.title: Title of the four-question flow that checks one item for free repairs.
auth.email.label: Placeholder and screen-reader name of the email box.
auth.email.savedLocal: Hover tooltip on an icon beside the email box: the email address is saved only on this device. Separate key from auth.name.savedLocal so the participle can agree with 'email address'.
auth.error.email: Error when the email is empty or malformed. The example address may be localised (it is only shown, never checked).
auth.error.name: Error when the first-name box is empty. 'shelf' = the saved list of things you own.
auth.fine:
HTML. Fine print under the form. Keep
and the tag; the linked words should read naturally both inside the sentence and on their own.
auth.help.default: Help line under the name and email boxes. 'Both' = the first name and the email. Also shown again after an error message is cleared.
auth.help.notYou: Help line for a returning visitor whose saved name and email are prefilled.
auth.meta.description: Search-result snippet. 'it' = Owed. 'shelf' = the saved list of things you own.
auth.meta.title: Browser tab title of the sign-in page. There is no account or password: the user only types a first name and email that stay in this browser. 'Owed' is the brand.
auth.name.label: Placeholder and screen-reader name of the first-name box.
auth.name.savedLocal: Hover tooltip on an icon beside the first-name box: the first name is saved only on this device.
auth.panel.label: Screen-reader name of the side panel with a video about Owed.
auth.panel.sub: 'cover' = warranty or repair protection; 'the claim' = the request the user sends to get it.
auth.panel.title: Short slogan over a video. 'cover' = warranty / repair protection the user is entitled to.
auth.ring.resume: Screen-reader name of a pause/play button for an animated ring of icons. Not currently on the page; kept for when it returns.
auth.sub: HTML. Keep the <strong> tags around the second sentence.
auth.submit.continueAs: Submit button for a returning visitor. {name} is the first name they typed before (any name, may start with a vowel). If your language changes the words before a vowel (French 'que' / 'qu''), choose wording that works for every name. Keep it short: it is a single-line button.
auth.title:
HTML. One sentence split over two lines by
; the part inside the span is coloured. Keep
and the span with its class; you may move the split to a natural point in your language.
catalog.age.months3: Tile in the add-item wizard answering when the item was bought (sentence case). The tiles are read in this order: months3, months9, months14, months22, months34, months60, months96, then a 'can't remember' tile. After saving, the item shows the matching engine.age.* phrase instead (e.g. 'a couple of months ago').
catalog.age.months96: See _note.catalog.age.months3. Follows 'Four to six years ago': more than six years ago.
catalog.category.applianceLarge: See _note.catalog.category.phone. Fridge, washing machine, dryer, dishwasher, oven.
catalog.category.applianceSmall: See _note.catalog.category.phone. Kettle, toaster, microwave, coffee machine.
catalog.category.bike: See _note.catalog.category.phone. A bicycle, e-bike or kick/electric scooter.
catalog.category.console: See _note.catalog.category.phone. A video games console (PlayStation, Xbox, Switch).
catalog.category.fallback: Category name for an item with no known category, in the same places as the other catalog.category.* names (see _note.catalog.category.phone).
catalog.category.other: See _note.catalog.category.phone. The last tile, for anything not listed.
catalog.category.outdoor: See _note.catalog.category.phone. Tents, sleeping bags, camping stoves, skis.
catalog.category.phone: Category name (sentence case) on a tile in the add-item wizard, in the item's facts line, on the print sheet and in the landing page's try-it box (lowercased there, in a sentence). When the person types no name, '{brand} {category}' is saved as the item's name ('Samsung Phone'), so a short noun without article works best. Applies to every catalog.category.* key.
catalog.category.toy: See _note.catalog.category.phone. Toys, strollers, car seats, cribs.
catalog.category.watch: See _note.catalog.category.phone. A watch, smartwatch or fitness tracker.
catalog.payment.fallback: Not shown today. Name for a payment method Owed does not know.
catalog.payment.mastercard: Payment method tile (see _note.catalog.payment.visa): a Mastercard credit card.
catalog.payment.unknown: Not shown today: the wizard puts its own wording on this tile. The person does not remember how they paid.
catalog.payment.visa: Payment method tile in the add-item wizard (sentence case). American Express and Discover tiles show the brand name alone and are not translated.
catalog.region.us: Not shown today (the region picker has its own labels). Name of a region whose consumer law Owed covers.
engine.age.aWhileAgo: When the item was bought, as a time phrase that already says 'ago'. Used when the person could not remember. Every engine.age.* phrase shows in three places and must read in all of them: alone, lowercase, in the item's facts line (category · brand · when); as {when} in engine.script.bought ('I bought X {when}.'); and in place of [date] in a rule's hint, where any preposition in front of [date] is removed ('failed on [date]' becomes 'failed about a year ago'). FR 'il y a quelque temps', ES 'hace tiempo'.
engine.age.aboutAYear: See _note.engine.age.aWhileAgo. Bought 13 to 17 months ago. FR 'il y a environ un an', ES 'hace aproximadamente un año'.
engine.age.aboutYears: See _note.engine.age.aWhileAgo. Plural: {n} is a whole number of years, 2 or more in practice. FR { one: 'il y a environ {n} an', other: 'il y a environ {n} ans' }, ES { one: 'hace aproximadamente {n} año', other: 'hace unos {n} años' }.
engine.age.fewMonths: See _note.engine.age.aWhileAgo. Bought within the last 3 months. FR 'il y a quelques mois', ES 'hace un par de meses'.
engine.age.underAYear: See _note.engine.age.aWhileAgo. Bought 4 to 12 months ago. FR 'il y a moins d'un an', ES 'hace menos de un año'.
engine.group.card: Group heading (see _note.engine.group.settlement): protection or extended warranty that comes with the credit card used to pay.
engine.group.program: Group heading (see _note.engine.group.settlement): a maker's own free repair or replacement programme for a known fault.
engine.group.retailer: Group heading (see _note.engine.group.settlement): the retailer's own return, warranty or guarantee policy. 'it' is the item.
engine.group.settlement: Heading over a group of rules on the results screen, naming where the help comes from: money a company had to put aside in a legal settlement for a known fault.
engine.group.statutory: Group heading (see _note.engine.group.settlement): rights consumer law gives the buyer.
engine.hint.amount: Fills the [amount] placeholder in the middle of a rule's own script hint, e.g. 'I was charged [amount]'. A noun phrase with its own article, spoken by the buyer ('my' card statement).
engine.pay.amex: See _note.engine.pay.visa. An American Express card: FR 'avec une carte American Express', ES 'con una tarjeta American Express'.
engine.pay.cash: See _note.engine.pay.visa. FR 'en espèces' (or 'comptant'), ES 'en efectivo': no 'avec' / 'con'.
engine.pay.debit: See _note.engine.pay.visa. FR (Canada) 'avec une carte de débit', ES 'con una tarjeta de débito'.
engine.pay.discover: See _note.engine.pay.visa. Discover is a card brand, not a verb.
engine.pay.mastercard: See _note.engine.pay.visa. FR 'avec une carte Mastercard', ES 'con una tarjeta Mastercard'.
engine.pay.visa: How the item was paid for, INCLUDING the preposition. Used as {pay} in engine.reason.paid ('you paid {pay}') and engine.script.boughtPaid ('... and paid {pay}.'). The preposition belongs here because it changes with the payment: FR 'avec une carte Visa' but 'en espèces', ES 'con una tarjeta Visa' but 'en efectivo'. Applies to every engine.pay.* key.
engine.reason.ageUnknown: See _note.engine.reason.brand. The rule has a time limit but the person does not remember when they bought the item; English drops the subject ('[it] depends'). 'it' is the item, gender unknown.
engine.reason.brand: One clause of the line under a rule that says why the rule matched the item. The app wraps the clauses as 'Why it matched: {clauses}.' (an app.* key). One to four engine.reason.* clauses are joined as a list: 'a, b and c' in English, your language's list pattern elsewhere ('a, b et c', 'a, b y c'). So every clause must stand on its own: lowercase start, no full stop, no pronoun pointing at another clause, and best without a comma of its own. These notes apply to every engine.reason.* key. {brand} is the item's brand name. English always writes 'a' here, even before a vowel ('it is a Apple item': a quirk kept as it is). FR e.g. 'c'est un produit {brand}', ES 'es un producto {brand}'.
engine.reason.brandUnnamed: See _note.engine.reason.brand. Practically never shown (a rule only matches on brand when the item has one). Means 'it is an item of that brand'.
engine.reason.covers: See _note.engine.reason.brand. Used alone when nothing more specific applies. 'it' is the rule (FR 'la règle', feminine), not the item.
engine.reason.floorPassed: See _note.engine.reason.brand. The minimum period the law guarantees is over, but national or local law can give more time, so asking is still worthwhile.
engine.reason.law: See _note.engine.reason.brand. The rule is consumer law with no time limit stated, and it applies whatever the manufacturer's warranty says.
engine.reason.paid: See _note.engine.reason.brand. The rule only covers some payment methods and the item was paid with one of them. {pay} is an engine.pay.* phrase with its own preposition ('with a Visa card'), so write 'you paid {pay}', never 'you paid with {pay}'.
engine.reason.payUnknown: See _note.engine.reason.brand. The rule depends on the payment method and the person does not remember how they paid; 'statement' is the card or bank statement.
engine.reason.windowClosing: See _note.engine.reason.brand. The time limit for claiming ends soon.
engine.reason.windowOpen: See _note.engine.reason.brand. 'the window' is the time limit for claiming under this rule (FR 'le délai', ES 'el plazo').
engine.script.bought: The claim message's second sentence when the item has NO typed name: {thing} is a full noun phrase with its own article from engine.thing.* ('un téléphone Samsung'), {when} an engine.age.* phrase, {broke} engine.script.broken or notBroken.
engine.script.boughtNamed: Used instead of engine.script.bought (outside English) when the visitor TYPED the item's name: {thing} is that name exactly as written, often a product label with a capital and no article ('Casque Sony WH-1000XM4', 'mon vieux frigo'), so the sentence must stay grammatical whatever it is. Owed puts it in parentheses after a neutral noun: 'J'ai acheté cet article ({thing}) {when}.' English never uses this key; its value just mirrors engine.script.bought.
engine.script.boughtPaid: As engine.script.bought, plus {pay}: an engine.pay.* phrase ('avec une carte Visa', 'en espèces').
engine.script.broken: Whole sentence that is {broke} in engine.script.bought / boughtPaid when the item is faulty. 'It' is the item, whose gender and number are unknown (it can be any name the person typed), so use a wording that needs no agreement (FR e.g. 'L'appareil ne fonctionne plus correctement.', ES e.g. 'Ha dejado de funcionar bien.').
engine.script.close: Last paragraph of the claim script: a question, then a thank-you, in one value. ES needs the opening '¿'; FR a narrow no-break space before '?'.
engine.script.hello: First paragraph of the claim script: the words a person reads out on the phone or pastes into an email to a company. Each engine.script.* value is one paragraph; the paragraphs are separated by a blank line and come in this order: hello, bought/boughtPaid, rule, serial (only when a serial number is known), the rule's own hint (only when it has one), close. Polite, formal register (vous / usted): the reader is a stranger at a company.
engine.script.notBroken: Whole sentence that is {broke} when the item still works (the person is checking before anything goes wrong). 'it' is the item, see _note.engine.script.broken. 'cover' means warranty or protection cover.
engine.script.rule: Third paragraph of the claim script. {title} is the rule's title in the rule's own language, which is English wherever the rule has no translation (e.g. 'Apple one-year limited warranty', 'Whirlpool one-year appliance warranty'). Nothing may agree with {title}. 'this' and 'covered' refer to the item, whose gender is unknown: prefer a wording that needs no agreement (FR 'couvert/couverte'). FR puts a no-break space before ':'.
engine.script.serial: Claim script paragraph shown only when the person entered a serial number. {serial} is that number as typed, e.g. 'C02XK0ABJG5H'.
engine.thing.apparel: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Clothing'. English prints the raw id 'apparel' (a quirk kept as it is); write the natural phrase: FR 'un vêtement {brand}', ES 'una prenda {brand}'.
engine.thing.applianceLarge: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Big appliance' (fridge, washing machine, oven). English prints the raw id 'appliance-large' and 'a appliance' (quirks kept as they are); write the natural phrase: FR 'un gros électroménager {brand}', ES 'un electrodoméstico grande {brand}'.
engine.thing.applianceSmall: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Small appliance' (kettle, toaster, coffee machine). English prints the raw id (a quirk kept as it is); write the natural phrase: FR 'un petit électroménager {brand}', ES 'un pequeño electrodoméstico {brand}'.
engine.thing.bag: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Bag or luggage'. FR 'un sac {brand}', ES 'un bolso {brand}' / 'una mochila {brand}'.
engine.thing.bike: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Bike or scooter'. FR 'un vélo {brand}', ES 'una bicicleta {brand}' (feminine).
engine.thing.camera: See _note.engine.thing.phone. FR 'un appareil photo {brand}', ES 'una cámara {brand}' (feminine).
engine.thing.console: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Games console'. FR 'une console {brand}' (feminine), ES 'una consola {brand}'.
engine.thing.footwear: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Shoes or boots'. English prints the raw id 'footwear' (a quirk kept as it is); write the natural phrase: FR 'une paire de chaussures {brand}', ES 'unos zapatos {brand}'.
engine.thing.furniture: See _note.engine.thing.phone. English needs 'piece of'; FR 'un meuble {brand}', ES 'un mueble {brand}'.
engine.thing.headphones: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Headphones or earbuds'. English needs 'pair of'; your language may not: FR 'un casque {brand}' or 'des écouteurs {brand}', ES 'unos auriculares {brand}'.
engine.thing.kitchen: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Cookware or kitchen' (pans, pots, knives); English guesses 'pan'. FR 'une poêle {brand}' or the more general 'un ustensile de cuisine {brand}', ES 'una sartén {brand}' or 'un utensilio de cocina {brand}'.
engine.thing.laptop: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Laptop or computer'. FR 'un ordinateur portable {brand}', ES 'un portátil {brand}' / 'una computadora portátil {brand}'.
engine.thing.mattress: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Mattress or bedding'. FR 'un matelas {brand}', ES 'un colchón {brand}'.
engine.thing.oldApplianceLarge: Not produced by the app today (a category id from an earlier version). Translate exactly like engine.thing.applianceLarge.
engine.thing.oldApplianceSmall: Not produced by the app today (a category id from an earlier version). Translate exactly like engine.thing.applianceSmall.
engine.thing.oldShoes: Not produced by the app today (a category id from an earlier version). Translate exactly like engine.thing.footwear.
engine.thing.oldTool: Not produced by the app today (a category id from an earlier version). Translate exactly like engine.thing.powerTool.
engine.thing.other: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Something else', and any item with no category. English prints 'a item' with no brand (a quirk kept as it is). FR 'un article {brand}' / 'un article', ES 'un artículo {brand}' / 'un artículo'.
engine.thing.outdoor: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Outdoor gear' (tents, sleeping bags, skis). English prints the raw id 'outdoor' (a quirk kept as it is); write the natural phrase: FR 'un équipement de plein air {brand}', ES 'un equipo para exteriores {brand}'.
engine.thing.phone: How the claim script names the item when the person gave it no name: {thing} in engine.script.bought / boughtPaid, and the [item] / [product] / [model] placeholder in a rule's own hint (e.g. 'My [item] stopped working'). Write a whole noun phrase with its article and the brand where your language puts it: EN 'a {brand} phone', FR 'un téléphone {brand}', ES 'un teléfono {brand}'. {brand} is a brand name (Apple, Samsung, De’Longhi). ENGLISH ONLY: the code turns the leading 'a' into 'an' when the brand starts with a vowel letter ('an Apple phone'); nothing is done to French or Spanish, so write the article your noun needs. Every engine.thing.<x> has a sibling engine.thing.<x>.noBrand: the same phrase with no brand. These notes apply to every engine.thing.* key.
engine.thing.phone.noBrand: engine.thing.phone with no brand: FR 'un téléphone', ES 'un teléfono'. English always writes 'a' here, even before a vowel.
engine.thing.powerTool: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Power tool'. English prints the raw id 'power-tool' (a quirk kept as it is); write the natural phrase: FR 'un outil électrique {brand}', ES 'una herramienta eléctrica {brand}' (feminine).
engine.thing.printer: See _note.engine.thing.phone. FR 'une imprimante {brand}', ES 'una impresora {brand}' (both feminine).
engine.thing.tablet: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Tablet or e-reader'. FR 'une tablette {brand}' (feminine).
engine.thing.toy: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Toy or baby gear'. FR 'un jouet {brand}', ES 'un juguete {brand}'.
engine.thing.tv: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'TV or monitor'. English prints the lowercase id 'tv' (a quirk kept as it is); write the natural noun: FR 'un téléviseur {brand}', ES 'un televisor {brand}'.
engine.thing.unlisted: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Not produced by the app today: a category id Owed has no words for. {word} is that id in lowercase English ('monitor'). Both slots must stay: FR e.g. 'un article {brand} ({word})', ES 'un artículo {brand} ({word})'.
engine.thing.vacuum: See _note.engine.thing.phone. A vacuum cleaner. FR 'un aspirateur {brand}', ES 'una aspiradora {brand}' (feminine).
engine.thing.watch: See _note.engine.thing.phone. Category 'Watch or tracker'. FR 'une montre {brand}' (feminine), ES 'un reloj {brand}' (masculine).

landing.try.heading.brand: Result card heading when only a brand was recognised. {brand} = the brand name.
landing.try.heading.label: Result card heading when only a category was recognised. {label} = category name in lowercase, {category} = the same name with its capitals. See landing.try.heading.labelBrand.
landing.try.heading.labelBrand: Heading of the result card after the visitor types what broke, when both a category and a brand were recognised (e.g. typed "sony headphones"). {label} = the category name in lowercase, e.g. "headphones or earbuds", "laptop or computer", "big appliance". {category} = the same name with its original capitals (use it where lowercase would be wrong, e.g. "TV or monitor"). {brand} = a brand name, e.g. "Sony". The category has no known gender or number and is often "X or Y", so avoid articles or adjectives that must agree with it: prefer a construction like "{brand}, {label}: ..." . English deliberately always says "A" here; do not copy that.
landing.try.heading.none: Result card heading when neither a category nor a brand was recognised in what the visitor typed.
landing.try.label: Hidden label of the search field: which item broke.
landing.try.line.card: Bullet point in the result card: extra warranty from the card used to pay.
landing.try.line.law: Bullet point in the result card: legal guarantee, which usually lasts longer than the printed warranty.
landing.try.line.maker: One of four bullet points in the result card after the visitor types what broke. Shown as HTML text; no markup needed.
landing.try.line.payouts: Bullet point in the result card: open payouts and free repair programmes for known faults.
landing.try.placeholder: Placeholder of the search field. Sony and Whirlpool are brand names: keep them, translate the product nouns. Ends with an ellipsis character.
landing.try.placeholderShort: The same placeholder on phones, where only about 150px is visible. Keep it very short.
landing.try.sub: Line under the result card heading: in the app, four questions narrow the list to the rules worth asking about.
landing.try.submit: Submit button of the search field. Keep it short.

store.demo.drill: See _note.store.demo.headphones. FR 'Perceuse sans fil DeWalt', ES 'Taladro inalámbrico DeWalt'.
store.demo.headphones: Name of a sample item on the demo shelf (app.html?demo=1), shown in the shelf, as the results title, in the claim script and in an email subject. It is saved once, in the language the demo is first opened in. Keep the brand and model exactly; place them where your language puts a brand: FR 'Casque Sony WH-1000XM4', ES 'Auriculares Sony WH-1000XM4'. Applies to every store.demo.* key.
store.demo.skillet: See _note.store.demo.headphones. FR 'Poêle en fonte Lodge', ES 'Sartén de hierro fundido Lodge'.
theme.dark: Screen-reader label of the theme toggle button. It is a toggle: its on/off state says whether the dark theme is on, so the label names the dark theme itself.
theme.toDark: Tooltip of the theme toggle while the light theme is on.
theme.toLight: Tooltip of the theme toggle while the dark theme is on.
